investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes advertise the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have exhausted their allocatable quota; the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also evaluated and found unhelpful (no evictable victims on the two eligible nodes, and affinity mismatch makes the other four ineligible regardless). Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remoteState value, causing a total contract gap for all four required evidence fields. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 144s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calls createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) which never returned a VM identity.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130515 — the check ran for ~130s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 125s unschedulable timeout reported in the message.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the two eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable units for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating all current consumers have equal or higher priority.

[Likely contributing] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), so the 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking total capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

[Possible] The kata-peerpods device plugin or VM provider on one or both eligible nodes may have stopped advertising the extended resource correctly, causing the node to report fewer available units than are physically present.

[Low probability] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than any single node can satisfy) could make the pod permanently unschedulable even on an otherwise healthy cluster.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes show available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure, the root cause is not simple capacity exhaustion and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If a subsequent eval run succeeds without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm is set to a value larger than the per-node maximum, the failure would be a misconfiguration rather than exhaustion — confirmed by comparing the request quantity against node Allocatable.

If the kata-peerpods device plugin logs show the nodes were advertising incorrect (deflated) capacity due to a plugin crash or restart, the root cause is plugin health rather than true VM slot exhaustion.
If only one of the three sibling checks had failed with this message, a transient race condition rather than full pool exhaustion would be more likely.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource Allocatable vs. Allocated ratio across all eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing earlier warning before full exhaustion.
Add an eval that checks the health and uptime of the kata-peerpods device plugin pods on all kata-capable nodes, catching plugin crashes before they manifest as scheduling failures.
Add an eval that verifies the minimum number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the cluster meets a defined floor, alerting if a node is drained or lost and the pool shrinks below safe capacity.

Consider adding a latency-only eval that attempts remote agent pod scheduling without waiting for full VM readiness, to distinguish scheduling failures from VM boot failures earlier in the timeout window.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the upstream pod scheduling failure prevented any agent from being created, which in turn caused the remote-agent-state check to produce zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing) and fail its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted by the eval runner for a remote agent is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this scheduling blockage: the agent pod never starts, so no agent identity or state is ever returned, and all required evidence fields remain absent.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval pod. This is the strongest explanation given the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across all three sibling checks.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets nodes with a specific label (e.g., a kata peer-pods node pool label), but 4 of 6 nodes no longer carry that label — possibly due to a node pool scaling event, node replacement, or label removal. This would reduce the schedulable node count from 6 to 2, compounding the resource exhaustion.

Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: the 6-node cluster may have insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to handle the eval probe's demand alongside any existing workloads, indicating a capacity planning gap rather than a transient exhaustion.

Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) did not fully terminate agent pods, those pods may be holding resource slots that prevent new scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes advertise the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have exhausted their allocatable quota; the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also evaluated and found unhelpful (no evictable victims on the two eligible nodes, and affinity mismatch makes the other four ineligible regardless). Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remoteState value, causing a total contract gap for all four required evidence fields. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 125s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 145s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 144s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the pod never reaching a running state.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calls createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) which never returned a VM identity.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130515 — the check ran for ~130s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 125s unschedulable timeout reported in the message.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the two eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable units for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating all current consumers have equal or higher priority.

[Likely contributing] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), so the 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking total capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

[Possible] The kata-peerpods device plugin or VM provider on one or both eligible nodes may have stopped advertising the extended resource correctly, causing the node to report fewer available units than are physically present.

[Low probability] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than any single node can satisfy) could make the pod permanently unschedulable even on an otherwise healthy cluster.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the upstream pod scheduling failure prevented any agent from being created, which in turn caused the remote-agent-state check to produce zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing) and fail its expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted by the eval runner for a remote agent is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this scheduling blockage: the agent pod never starts, so no agent identity or state is ever returned, and all required evidence fields remain absent.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval pod. Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets nodes with a specific label (e.g., a kata peer-pods node pool label), but 4 of 6 nodes no longer carry that label — possibly due to a node pool scaling event, node replacement, or label removal. This would reduce the schedulable node count from 6 to 2, compounding the resource exhaustion.

Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: the 6-node cluster may have insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to handle the eval probe's demand alongside any existing workloads, indicating a capacity planning gap rather than a transient exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any remote agent VM from being created.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and no agent VM is ever started. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity or configuration problem localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in production-api; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was also attempted and found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are full. If the affinity rules were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling could succeed.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, which may be insufficient for the current load or for concurrent eval runs. A scale-out or node addition would resolve this.

LOWER — Transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads (e.g., from other users or parallel eval runs) may have temporarily exhausted the 2 kata nodes. If capacity freed up shortly after the eval window, this would be intermittent rather than persistent.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and returns all required evidence fields, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion condition.

If the pod spec's node affinity or selector rules are found to target more than 2 nodes (i.e., the 4 non-matching nodes are eligible in principle), then the affinity configuration is not the bottleneck and the diagnosis shifts entirely to resource exhaustion on the 2 kata nodes.
If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes while remote-agent-runtime continues to fail, the scheduling layer is not the shared root cause and a check-specific issue must be investigated.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources at the time of the failure, the resource exhaustion hypothesis is disproved and a node-level driver or admission webhook issue should be investigated instead.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each eligible node and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check eval that submits a dry-run pod (using --dry-run=server or equivalent) for the remote agent pod spec and asserts it would be schedulable, catching node affinity and resource exhaustion issues before a full agent creation is attempted.
Add a cluster node inventory eval that asserts at least N nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and match the remote agent pod's affinity selector, alerting on node count drops.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create at a lower frequency with a shorter timeout to detect scheduling degradation earlier in the eval pipeline, before the full runtime check is attempted.
